For sorting 10,000,000 `double` values sampled from a uniform distribution, `std::sort` will consistently outperform a hand-written QuickSort in terms of both execution time and memory safety. In competitive programming and systems programming contexts, `std::sort` is the default choice for general-purpose sorting unless specific constraints (e.g., stability, limited memory, or external sorting) dictate otherwise.

*   **`std::sort`**: Implemented as **Introsort** (a hybrid algorithm) in most standard library implementations (e.g., libstdc++, MSVC STL). It begins with QuickSort but switches to HeapSort if the recursion depth exceeds $2 \log_2 N$. This guarantees **$O(N \log N)$** worst-case time complexity.
*   **Custom QuickSort**: A naive implementation has **$O(N^2)$** worst-case time complexity.
